title: A personal account of negotiating a contract rate
why: Personal career anecdote about switching from salary to hourly contracting; no transferable technical lesson beyond the author's own situation.

title: Personal impressions of the JET teaching programme
why: Anecdotal opinion about the JET programme and its motives; largely personal experience rather than verifiable insider knowledge.

title: Why Rust 2018 changes absolute path resolution
why: Explains the mental model behind confusing use and extern crate behavior, and why absolute paths now begin with the crate name.

title: Requests for full text of a Google China article
why: Pastes a newspaper article about Google's China withdrawal; no original analysis or explanation in the comment itself.

title: Rebuttal of an article on innate conscience
why: Argumentative critique of a New Atheist essay; it disputes a philosophical framing rather than teaching a durable insight.

title: Personal account of living and working in Japan
why: Personal anecdote about fluency, work and discrimination in Japan; experience-based but without a broadly useful lesson.

title: Einstein quotes on technology and human heart
why: Collects quotations about technology, ethics and religion; a moral argument with no technical explanation.

title: Why broadcast graphics avoid pure black and white
why: Legal gamut headroom and careful filtering prevent crawl and strobing on NTSC; hand-fitting pixels rarely beats good filtering.

title: Skeptical valuation argument about Tesla profitability
why: Speculative market argument comparing Tesla with automakers; reasoned opinion about stock price rather than a lasting technical insight.

title: Good Will Hunting scene about working for the NSA
why: Quotes a film monologue on surveillance ethics; a moral argument rather than explanatory knowledge.

title: Advice to build a portfolio instead of a degree
why: Opinionated career advice from personal success; sensible but generic and not grounded in explanation or expertise.

title: Skepticism about Stradivarius sound and placebo
why: Opinionated skepticism about violin and audio claims; it argues about perception rather than explaining how instruments actually work.

title: Personal account of working part time as freelancer
why: Lifestyle anecdote about choosing part-time freelance work and financial comfort; personal, with no broadly useful lesson.

title: Argument against leaving university to start a company
why: Opinionated career advice mixing anecdote and speculation about startups, ageism and networks; not grounded in explanation.

title: Most common Android app permissions by app share
why: First-hand static analysis data: INTERNET appears in 92.9 percent of apps, network state 83 percent, storage access about 60 percent.

title: Cold chills, ASMR and frisson are distinct phenomena
why: Explains three different sensory responses by trigger and emotional character, noting ASMR and frisson affect roughly 3 to 10 percent of people.

title: Choose boring mature tools for business growth
why: Practical but generic advice to avoid trendy technology; it is opinion rather than a detailed, verifiable explanation.

title: Argument that technology cannot fix emissions alone
why: Opinionated climate argument with a rant about consumer behaviour and power plants; debate rather than explanation.

title: Complaints about Firefox slowness and tab management
why: User observations and complaints about browser performance and workflow; anecdotal, without a verified explanation or fix.

title: How rice preparation determines sushi quality
why: Washing removes starch, polishing removes bran, and exact water ratios control texture; each step strongly affects gluey or mushy results.

title: Advice on finding friends through shared activities
why: Personal advice about friendship and alienation; supportive and sensible, but it is emotional guidance rather than technical knowledge.

title: Critique of TSA effectiveness and airport security
why: Opinion on TSA effectiveness with personal travel memories and political sentiment; a debate rather than a lesson.

title: Counter-reading of The Social Network characters
why: Subjective film review arguing about character motives; interpretive opinion with no technical or factual lesson.

title: Constitutional options for challenging surveillance laws
why: Political and legal argument about the Snowden leaks; an opinion on constitutional strategy rather than verified explanation.

title: Personal reflection on childhood dreams and laziness
why: Personal reflection on school tracks and missed ambitions; emotional content without a broadly useful lesson.

title: What quantum computers can and cannot do yet
why: Shor's algorithm would break RSA only with many entangled qubits; D-Wave's annealing design is unconventional and far from general quantum computation.

title: Cheap free tooling let the web outpace enterprise stacks
why: Enterprise suites cost thousands and needed heavy training; free Linux, MySQL and PHP let small teams build and ship, which drove web adoption.

title: Why containers are process isolation, not a fad
why: A container is essentially a process, so it is a useful abstraction; serverless requires rewriting apps and cannot hold long-lived server connections.

title: Personal account of despair and American healthcare
why: Emotional personal account and political complaint about healthcare and society; important to the writer but not an instructive technical insight.

title: Rebuttal of claims about Twitter and centralization
why: Argumentative response to a post on decentralization; debates the framing of platforms rather than teaching a verifiable mechanism.

title: Why streetcars were profitable and modern transit is not
why: Streetcars opened new land as real estate plays and carried dense daily ridership; cars and decentralization removed both drivers of profit.

title: Sowell's view of left and right as human nature
why: Summarizes a political framework of human nature views; contested ideological argument rather than neutral explanation of a mechanism.

title: Complaint about Filament's heavy build prerequisites
why: Reacts to the build requirements listed for Filament, noting the gap between small-dependency claims and a long prerequisite list.

title: Why Amazon struggles to stop counterfeit sellers
why: No global authenticity lookup exists and banned sellers reincorporate; buy from Amazon itself or established brands to reduce counterfeit risk.

title: What developers miss about Adobe Flash workflows
why: Nostalgic list of features from Flash such as nested clips and content-first workflow; personal preference rather than a transferable explanation.

title: Personal account of a hacker's time in prison
why: Personal story about prison life and making phones work; entertaining, but the lesson is personal rather than broadly instructive.

title: Early attempts to show light has a finite speed
why: Traces Alhazen, Bacon, Beeckman and Galileo; Galileo's lantern experiment failed to detect delay, showing light's speed must be extraordinarily high.

title: Read the heap dump before guessing at causes
why: A team had spent weeks on out-of-memory errors without reading the heap; the dump immediately showed session objects accumulating and not being cleaned.

title: Test of a new search engine's result quality
why: Lists poor results from four test queries to argue ranking is the problem; a review of one product rather than a general lesson.

title: Opinion on sexism and gender roles in the US
why: Personal observations and sociological speculation about gender in engineering and culture; opinion without verifiable evidence.

title: Speculation on government uses of bitcoin
why: Speculative essay about surveillance and taxation of bitcoin accounts; interesting musing, but not grounded in technical explanation.

title: Opinion on python's rise and its inconsistencies
why: Opinionated complaint about Python's runtime quirks and newcomer audience; subjective critique rather than a teachable mental model.

title: Personal reply about addiction, judgment and stigma
why: Emotional reply about addiction, family abandonment and social judgment; personal experience and opinion, not a technical lesson.

title: Personal account of symptoms after early covid
why: Personal medical anecdote describing symptoms and doctor visits; experience-based but not a verifiable explanation for others.

title: Existing ways people already speed up Python
why: Lists psyco, PyPy, Numba, Cython, Pyston and numpy as acceleration routes, arguing that speed is hard and already receiving serious work.

title: Personal take on Mormon culture in Utah
why: Personal sociological view of Mormon culture, women and MLMs; opinion from lived experience rather than a technical or factual lesson.

title: Interviewers screen to avoid the worst hires
why: Experienced managers aim to avoid bad hires rather than pick the best, so soft interview questions mainly test whether a candidate seems normal and reliable.

title: Personal reflection on sleep anxiety and a website
why: Personal story about insomnia and how a sleep statistic fed anxiety; a reflection on the author's own experience.

title: Story of a suspicious NAS bought from Amazon
why: Anecdote about receiving a used, Chinese-language device from a third-party seller; an entertaining story without a broad lesson.

title: How 1990s GSM networks routed and billed calls
why: BSCs connect cell sites, MSCs route to SS7, HLRs track phone registration and feed billing; text messaging grew from a value-added service into a core one.

title: Criticism of Amazon's culture and big-name careers
why: Opinion on Amazon's culture and the prestige of big-company jobs; a career argument with personal grievances rather than explanation.

title: Why hiring processes filter mass applications
why: A flood of 500 applicants in one day made 30-minute calls infeasible, so employers must filter cheaply; boot-camp resumes looked identical.

title: Opinion that democracies allocate resources better
why: Broad political opinion asserting democracies decide better over time; a contested claim presented without rigorous supporting evidence.

title: Opinion that Linux cannot be automotive grade
why: Experienced engineer's opinion that Linux's tradeoffs prevent automotive-grade stability; a judgment call rather than a detailed technical explanation.

title: Useful but overlooked Unix command-line tools
why: A practical list of tools such as bsdiff, par2, pv, mktemp, glark and lshw, with a short description of what each one does.

title: Personal take on Silicon Valley towns to live in
why: Dated personal impressions of towns near Silicon Valley; local opinion about housing and nightlife with no lasting technical value.

title: Contrarian argument about climate change solutions
why: Opinionated rant about climate science and the futility of action, mostly a debate about the commenter's stance rather than an explanation.

title: Why autofocus and custom file inputs often hurt users
why: Autofocus disrupts desktop Space-key scrolling and pops mobile keyboards, and custom file inputs often break; only autofocus after explicit user intent.

title: Why linked-list strings are slow versus packed arrays
why: Each character in a linked-list string needs two pointers that can scatter across memory, hurting cache use; a packed C-style array avoids this overhead.

title: Personal account of homelessness in Central LA
why: Personal neighborhood experience and moral reflection on homelessness and safety; emotional and political rather than an instructive explanation.

title: Advice on equity expectations and hiring offers
why: Opinion on equity compensation and hiring conversations; sensible framing but largely subjective advice rather than verifiable expertise.

title: Calculating whether 8K is visible at normal distance
why: At 6.5 feet from a 65-inch TV, 20/12.5 vision resolves about 3840 pixels across, matching 4K; low-contrast video hides even that.

title: Rant against Chrome dropping Manifest V2
why: Emotional attack on Google's extension policy and its handling of the WebExtensions group; expresses anger rather than explaining the technical change.

title: Cached array length and critique of a Closure review
why: Shows caching array length matters in tight loops, and that Closure's own array code already caches it where it counts, refuting a naive critique.

title: Personal account of visa and consulate delays
why: Personal story about a fiancée's visa renewal and consulate delays; a sympathetic account of one case rather than a general lesson.

title: Argument that textbooks should cost far less
why: Opinionated argument about textbook prices and lawsuits, with an analogy from Don Quixote; advocacy rather than explanation.

title: Why Opera lost focus despite brilliant engineering
why: Insider account: a portable engine and OEM dependence slowed development, and weak focus on design undermined Opera's browser strategy.

title: Why experts write instructions that novices cannot follow
why: Experts forget how much they know, so simple-seeming instructions omit steps; testing instructions on busy newcomers reveals the missing parts.

title: Promotion of AGI research over Chomsky's views
why: Argues AGI research is ignored and promotes a specific project; partisan advocacy rather than a balanced explanation of the field.

title: Rebuttal of claims about New York tech costs
why: Argues with a writer's cost-of-living numbers and housing options; opinion with anecdotes, not a generalizable technical lesson.

title: Rebuttal of an essay comparing Rails with Microsoft
why: Lengthy argumentative response disputing a blog post's cost and hardware comparison; a critique of rhetoric rather than a clear explanation.

title: Personal list of books and comics read
why: Shares personal reading and RSS subscriptions; a list of personal preferences rather than a curated resource with explanation.

title: Ayn Rand-inspired argument on bank governance
why: Political and philosophical argument about incentives and CEO accountability in 2007 banks; an ideological opinion rather than factual explanation.

title: Opinion on Putin's worldview and power
why: Speculative political opinion about the mentality behind Putin's decisions; contested interpretation without verifiable evidence.

title: Choosing a practical city bike in the US
why: Look for chain guards, racks, fender mounts and generator lights; US transport bikes often beat Dutch-style imports for American cities.

title: Excerpt from a screenplay about surveillance
why: Quotes a film script scene about state power and terrorism; fiction and political commentary rather than explanatory knowledge.

title: Complaint about citizenship-based taxation for US expats
why: Personal grievance about reporting burdens for citizens born abroad; sympathetic but mainly complaint rather than a practical guide.

title: Table of HN submission counts by domain
why: Raw table of submission counts and points per domain; data without interpretation or a clear explanation of its meaning.

title: Opinion that modern software tooling is easier
why: Personal reflection that free compilers and databases make development easier than before; an opinion more than a detailed explanation.

title: How cost cutting breeds procedure-heavy jobs
why: Cheap unskilled hires need manuals, each error adds checks, and procedures grow until skilled staff leave; a plausible mental model of organizational decay.

title: Why 1990s scripting languages were inherently slow
why: Dynamic typing, boxing and hash-table everything make such languages fundamentally slow, so JIT gains like asm.js reveal what was left on the table.

title: Reply to feedback on a toy language design
why: Conversational reply about a personal language design with comments on async and comments; replies only make sense in context.

title: Facebook's data export omits photos you are tagged in
why: The Graph API misreports tagged photos and blocks export, so the author scraped them with authenticated cookies; first-hand reverse engineering of the gap.

title: Why large companies use standardized coding interviews
why: Huge candidate volume rules out take-home tasks or day-long trials, so standardized coding and design interviews scale, despite imperfect signal.

title: Why published synthesis yields are hard to reproduce
why: Novel syntheses often drop from grams to micrograms, and reported yields like 75 percent can be unreproducible even by experienced chemists.

title: Personal story about a buggy Android update
why: Personal story about a firmware bug that garbled video audio and battery life; a frustrating anecdote without a broadly generalizable lesson.

title: Opinion on TJ high school admissions changes
why: Personal opinion on dropping an admissions test at a magnet school; policy debate with a personal memoir rather than a technical lesson.

title: Frustration with buzzwords and overengineering
why: Venting about colleagues chasing buzzwords like hadoop for small internal systems; a relatable complaint with no detailed explanation.

title: Name-dropping the notable engineers at Google
why: Lists famous engineers and anecdotes about Google's culture; impressive names but little explanation of how any work actually functioned.

title: Argument about population growth and Bay Area density
why: Quantitative but argumentative reply about density and water in the Bay Area; a debate framed around a position rather than neutral explanation.

title: Why low-frequency spectrum matters for wireless coverage
why: Sub-1GHz signals travel farther and penetrate buildings better; T-Mobile lacked it, limiting coverage and delaying its LTE rollout.

title: Personal account of depression and recovery
why: Emotional personal account of depression, isolation and recovery; supportive and sincere, but not a technical or factual lesson.

title: Why intermittent solar still needs fossil backup
why: Solar output is free but intermittent, so conventional plants must stay on standby for the remaining demand, and their costs do not disappear.

title: Detailed feedback on a spreadsheet analysis product
why: Product feedback on installer, scaling and workflow for a spreadsheet tool; useful to its maker but tied to one product.

title: Why engineering students outsource projects in India
why: Universities require external projects, but most lack industry links or supervision, so non-software fields have few real projects to offer students.

title: Historical account of Turkish politics and AKP
why: Partisan political history of Turkey shared from Facebook; a one-sided narrative about contested events rather than neutral explanation.

title: Playful list of free activities for friends
why: Whimsical list of inexpensive activities such as parks and karaoke; entertaining and personal, with no technical or factual lesson.

title: Argument for personal freedom in programming choices
why: Opinion that people may pick their tools but should not impose complexity on others; a philosophy of programming rather than a concrete explanation.

title: Build a strong math foundation before a PhD
why: Pure math teaches stating and proving theorems, the core skill for producing research that is new, correct and significant; Knuth's critique of PhD training supports it.

title: Product pitch for a no-tracker knowledge website
why: Promotional description of a knowledge site's design choices and VC avoidance; a product pitch rather than a teachable explanation.
